Class Vision

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.subsystems.vision.Vision
All Implemented Interfaces:
Subsystem
public class Vision extends Object implements Subsystem
FM's multi-source localization testbed: up to three Limelights and three Orin/PhotonVision cameras, each gated on its own and each logged well enough to compare after the fact.

Every loop

  1. Every source reads its device into logged inputs (PoseSource.update()), whether or not it is enabled.
  2. Every source gates every observation and logs the verdict and reason.
  3. PoseFusion applies each source's accepted measurements to that source's shadow track, and to the robot's fused pose if the source is enabled and its fusion policy allows it right now (see below).
  4. While disabled, the best Limelight's MegaTag1 seeds the heading and translation of every track. While enabled, the gross-heading safety net can re-seed once a camera has disagreed with the gyro badly for a full second.

Fusion policy (from the 2026 code)

  • Limelights fuse while enabled only in teleop, or in auto while the path asks for pose updates or the robot is launching (FM's main).
  • Every chassis Limelight fuses, not just the best one (offseason: the estimator already weights each by its std-devs).
  • MegaTag1 until the disabled seed is confirmed, MegaTag2 after (offseason, switchable at Vision/ChassisUseMT2).
  • The Orin cameras fuse whenever enabled and the robot is enabled. They start disabled: they are logged and shadowed, but do not move the robot pose until someone flips /Localization/Sources/<name>/Enabled on the dashboard.

Not ported from the offseason branch: the placement-heading vote and the two-camera consensus heading correction (both need the offseason bot's camera geometry to be meaningful), and everything turret-camera specific.

    • triggerRewindCaptureForAllCameras

      public void triggerRewindCaptureForAllCameras(double seconds)
      Saves the last seconds of the rewind buffer of each FM Limelight: video plus every frame's results, reviewable frame by frame afterwards. Rewind is a Limelight 4 feature; the camera writes the capture to its own storage, which survives a power cycle (checked 2026-10-16), so the robot can be powered off after a match.

      Not the SystemCore's own cameras: their "camera storage" is the robot controller's internal disk, which LogStorage is keeping free.

      Parameters:
      seconds - how much to save, at most 165
